craft_problem: Writing anger through melodramatic cliches (screaming, shouting, slamming doors, veins bulging) instead of high-tension restraint.
viewer_problem: Writers know their angry scenes sound like soap operas or temper tantrums.
bad_example: She was furious at him for lying.
transformation: Ground lethal anger in chilling domestic composure and precise object manipulation.
desired_learning: Dangerous anger lowers its voice and organizes the cutlery. Restraint carries more menace than shouting.
primary_keyword: how to write anger in fiction
search_intent_title: How to Write Anger Without Screaming
novelty_reason: First dedicated anger/fury craft teardown. Shifts emotional vocabulary from loud theatrics to domestic chilling stillness.
